# Showing another app's records

Two Protobase apps, where the shop's admin app shows the service desk's tickets with its own pages, sidebar and links.

Sam runs a web shop, and its customers' questions land in the company's service desk, a Protobase app of its own. When a customer calls about an order, Sam's people look the order up in the shop's admin app, then open the desk in another tab to find the customer's ticket. They want the tickets in the shop's admin app, next to the orders: a list, each ticket's page, the open ones in the sidebar, and a status they can change. The desk's agents keep working in the desk.

This guide makes the desk's tickets a [remote resource](../reference/remote-resources.md) of the shop: the shop draws them with its own pages, while the desk keeps the data, the rules and the views. Nothing is copied and nothing is proxied: the shop's admin app reads the desk's API with the shop's own sign-in.

## 1. Two apps

You need two Protobase projects, each with its own database, its own [admin store](../reference/auth.md#admin-store) and a user: the from-scratch preset (`tests/apps/scratch` in the repository) is enough for both. Each runs on its own origin; this guide runs them side by side on one machine:

| | `PROTOBASE_URL` in its `.env` | Started with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The service desk | `http://localhost:4720` | `protobase dev --port 4720` |
| The shop | `http://localhost:4710` | `protobase dev --port 4710` |

`PROTOBASE_URL` matters here: it is the issuer of each app's tokens, and the desk will recognise the shop's tokens by it.

The shop has its orders. The desk has tickets and their notes:

```ts
// desk: config/tickets/data.ts
import { f, resource } from '@protobase/schema'

type Caller = { user: { roles: string[] } }
const deskOnly = (ctx: unknown) => (ctx as Caller).user.roles.includes('admin')

export const tickets = resource('tickets')
  .table('tickets')
  .fields({
    id: f.integer().readOnly().filterable().sortable(),
    title: f.text().filterable().sortable(),
    customer_email: f.text().filterable(),
    status: f.enum(['open', 'waiting', 'closed']).filterable().sortable(),
    updated_at: f.timestamp().readOnly().filterable().sortable(),
  })
  .primaryKey((r) => r.id)
  .search((r) => [r.title, r.customer_email])
  .access({ delete: deskOnly })

export const ticketNotes = resource('ticket_notes')
  .table('ticket_notes')
  .fields({
    id: f.integer().readOnly().filterable().sortable(),
    ticket_id: f.relation('tickets').filterable(),
    body: f.text(),
    created_at: f.timestamp().readOnly().sortable(),
  })
  .primaryKey((r) => r.id)
  .access({ delete: deskOnly })
```

Only the desk's own admins delete: the [access rule](../reference/access.md) holds for everyone who reaches the desk's API, the shop's people included.

```ts
// desk: config/tickets/ui.ts
import { l, view } from '@protobase/schema'
import type { ticketNotes, tickets } from './data'

const recent = { status: 'status', tones: { open: 'warning', waiting: 'neutral', closed: 'success' }, orderBy: 'updated_at desc' } as const

export const ticketsView = view<typeof tickets>('tickets')
  .title((r) => r.title)
  .names({ singular: 'Ticket', plural: 'Tickets' })
  .nav({ group: 'Support', recent })
  .fields((r) => ({ customer_email: r.customer_email.label('Customer'), status: r.status.format('badge'), updated_at: r.updated_at.label('Changed').format('relative') }))
  .list((r) => ({ columns: [r.title, r.customer_email, r.status, r.updated_at], sort: [[r.updated_at, 'desc']] }))
  .filters((r, w) => [w.facets(r.status)])
  .layout((r) => [
    l.section('Ticket', [r.title, r.customer_email, r.status]),
    l.related('Notes', { resource: 'ticket_notes', field: 'ticket_id', sort: 'created_at desc', columns: ['body', 'created_at'], empty: 'No notes yet.' }),
  ])

export const ticketNotesView = view<typeof ticketNotes>('ticket_notes').nav({ hidden: true })
```

That is the desk's admin app as its agents use it. Nothing in it knows about the shop yet.

## 2. The desk lets the shop's people in

The shop's admin app will call the desk's API from the browser, with the token the shop gave the signed-in person. The desk needs to accept two things: that token, and calls from the shop's origin.

The token: list the shop as a trusted app in the desk's `authenticate`, and say what the shop's roles are at the desk. The origin: the shop's admin app runs on `http://localhost:4710`, so the desk answers [CORS](../reference/api.md#cors) for it:

```ts
// desk: protobase.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@protobase/config'

export default defineConfig({
  auth: { roles: ['admin'] },
  authenticate: {
    tenant: 1,
    // The shop's admins sign in at the shop; the desk takes the shop's tokens and calls them `shop` here.
    apps: [{ issuer: 'http://localhost:4710', roles: { admin: 'shop' }, tenant: 1 }],
  },
  // The shop's admin app, on its own origin, calls this API from the browser.
  cors: ['http://localhost:4710'],
})
```

The desk now checks a token from the shop against the shop's keys, at `http://localhost:4710/api/auth/jwks`. Its holder is `shop` at the desk, never the desk's `admin`, so the `deskOnly` rule keeps tickets from being deleted from the shop; a shop user with any other role is refused. The [reference](../reference/remote-resources.md#signing-in-at-the-source) has the details, such as the ids those users get.

`protobase dev` reloads the desk.

## 3. The shop draws the tickets

The shop lists the desk as a source, with the resources it draws from it:

```ts
// shop: protobase.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@protobase/config'

export default defineConfig({
  auth: { roles: ['admin'] },
  authenticate: { tenant: 1 },
  remoteResources: [{ url: 'http://localhost:4720/api/v1', label: 'Service desk', resources: ['tickets', 'ticket_notes'] }],
})
```

`url` is the desk's resources API, and `label` its name when the shop's people cannot reach it. The notes are there because a ticket's page lists them: what the shop does not draw, it does not show. A platform that runs the shop can set the same list in `PROTOBASE_SOURCES`, without touching the shop's code:

```sh
PROTOBASE_SOURCES='[{"url":"http://localhost:4720/api/v1","label":"Service desk","resources":["tickets","ticket_notes"]}]'
```

Had the shop a resource or page called `tickets` of its own, it would now refuse to start, naming both: `/tickets` can only be one thing.

## 4. The tickets in the shop

Sign in to the shop. The sidebar has a Support group with Tickets and the desk's recent tickets under it, each with its status; `/tickets` is the desk's list, with its columns, its status filter and its search, and the breadcrumbs read "Support › Tickets":

A ticket opens at `/tickets/1`, with its notes from the desk, and the trail back to the list. Change the status and Save: the shop's admin app writes it to the desk with the ticket's ETag, under the desk's rules, and the ticket moves in the sidebar. The global search in the top bar finds tickets too.

(The stories run on made-up data, with a summary section the next section describes.)

Behind it, the shop's admin app read the desk's `/api/meta` with the shop's token, kept the tickets and notes, and placed them as the desk's view says. Every list and save went straight from the browser to the desk.

## 5. A view for the shop's people

"Support" is how the desk's agents think of tickets. In the shop they are about customers, and only the open ones matter in the sidebar. The desk decides what the shop's people see, so it gives the role it gave them, `shop`, a [view of its own](../reference/ui-config.md#actions-and-views-per-role):

```ts
// desk: config/tickets/ui.ts
// What the shop's people see: the tickets of their customers, next to the shop's orders, and the open ones first.
export const shopTicketsView = ticketsView
  .forRoles(['shop'])
  .names({ singular: 'Customer ticket', plural: 'Customer tickets' })
  .nav({ group: 'Sales', recent: { ...recent, filter: 'status != "closed"' } })
```

After a reload, "Customer tickets" sits in the shop's own Sales group, under Orders, and its recent tickets are the ones still open. The desk's agents still see Support › Tickets.

## 6. When the desk is down

Stop the desk and reload the shop. The orders work as before. The tickets stay in the sidebar, under "Service desk" and marked, and `/tickets` says what is wrong, with a way to try again:

Start the desk again and press **Try again**: the tickets are back. The same happens when the desk answers but does not accept the shop's sign-in, for instance when its `apps` does not list the shop, with the desk's own reason.

## Custom sections

The desk's views can name [custom components](../reference/custom-components.md), such as a timeline of the ticket with `l.custom(TicketTimeline)`. The shop draws them by name from its [plugins](../reference/plugins.md), so the desk ships them as a plugin, built with `protobase build-plugin` and served wherever the shop's browser can load it, and the shop lists it with the source, for instance:

```sh
PROTOBASE_PLUGINS='http://localhost:4720/plugins/desk/plugin.json'
```

Inside, the component reads the ticket with `useLayoutRecord()`, and `useList` and `useRecord` read the desk for the desk's resources. Without the plugin, the shop draws the component's fallback in its place and everything else of the ticket.
